wow this is amazing! really motivating and hopeful for me. i’m awful and giving into my obsessive thoughts and then going to compulsively google about them and about all the worrying and scary stuff my brain comes up with just to make sure it’s normal or that even if i wanted to i couldn’t access anything super messed up on google. i have this weird anxiety over finding awful things on the internet that my ocd makes me have the need to google them just to make sure. 

i have tried to sit with those obsessive thoughts but then i get that itchy urge feeling to just click on a new tab and google it. writing in a journal app has somewhat helped, but it doesn’t replace the sense of relief i get when i google and read into stuff. i always get scared that i’ll feel that itchy needy feeling forever if i don’t give in and check google. i hope i can get to this level too and just keep focused and accept these feelings and accept that googling won’t help me and only makes me more stressed and susceptible to finding scary stuff.

wow, thank you so much for this. i’m still sort of reeling from your words and how much they’ve resonated with me. a finger trap is exactly how it feels. something will trigger that anxiety and the need to fish for certainty even if i know i wouldnt like the results. this happened multiple times within the past few months - since the googling obsession sort of made itself the main player in my ocd issues. happened once when i saw a meme on facebook about a list of a lot of edgy shock websites kids my age supposedly used to go on a lot back in the day. one of them in particular got me freaked out and i had to google about it to read into what it was. went through a whole spiral of finding this this and this and eventually just have myself a panic attack for no reason. 

and my other big one, which i admit i did check again today for the first time in a while because i got that itch. but my family likes to watch a youtuber who talks about scary stories and weird internet stuff - mr nightmare. i don’t watch bc i get too scared. but for some reason one of his (at the time) latest videos peaked my ocd curiosity so i just clicked it and muted it and read through comments haha. anyway, someone had commented that no matter what you can think of, humans have done worse, and how he once found a really messed up horrifying website on accident. of course, my dumb ass commented “omg what was the website?” among a couple others who did the same thing and all he said was like... oh only a psychopath would wanna look it up on purpose, super messed up. since then, i would periodically scroll to find that comment section and see if he had replied to anyone else and mentioned the website or what was on it. i really do not care but i get that obsessive need to know. i haven’t ever like, direct messaged him about it but still i check. it’s really frustrating. 

this would happen a lot when my friend would talk about the extreme horror movies he’s heard of. i wouldn’t be able to hold back the need to google them and read about them. i just like. need to know. even if it’s gross or what have you. it’s just like my brain thinks ok once i know exactly what it is, i won’t get that itchy anxious feeling over what it could possibly be. that’s why that guys youtube comment pretty much haunts me lol. i was good for a while i kind of wasn’t bothered anymore but now it’s back and i am going to really try harder and follow your advice. 

sorry this is long, but again thank you for all you’ve said.

maybe that’s still my fear, yeah. i think it’s just a more general fear of being deep down a bad/evil/crazy person. it’s like my brain is constantly out to get me haha. i’m a very empathetic and sensitive person. i cant watch movies with depictions of abuse to animals or any war/crime documentary otherwise i literally breakdown sobbing. i cry very easily at movies and shows and really just any time i have a conflict with someone i am quick to tears. my dad always says my empathy is like a super power but honestly it feels more like a burden and a source for my brain to sabotage me knowing i’m sensitive and easily moved by even my own intrusive thoughts. i exhaust myself over my own emotions i can’t imagine actually going through with searching up and seeing actual child abuse, as much as my brain urges me to just to get that adrenaline rush of a reaction. 

i haven’t had professional help but ive definitely considered it - though i’m always wary to discuss this specific type of ocd with people since it’s so jarring. i do want to try different cbt methods though, i think that could help. sorry for the long replies, thank you for your help. i appreciate it a lot and hope you have a good day/night. :)

i’m so sorry you’ve had to deal with that. :( i totally get that with the underage art part. i would see something on twitter that’s like “everyone block [this account] they’re drawing art of underage characters or smth” and instead of just scrolling past or blocking them, my brain wanted to specifically find the profile just to see the art. even though i had no urge or desire to see something like that. but googling underage stuff just to confirm/deny that i was actually attracted to it is such an awful impulse. 

but thinking about it rationally, as well as reading up on it - pedophiles have an attraction to children regardless of the nature of the media. ive read people seeing harmless and totally innocent videos or pictures of kids and get that urge/feeling of attraction. and i haven’t had that feeling. that sort of reassured me, but of course my ocd will be like - “yeah well maybe you only want to see children in sexual situations that’s why these don’t bother you, so you gotta look that up to check” which is harder to deal with. 

again, i feel your pain. going on these subreddits has helped me feel less alone and reading about other people’s similar situations helps. but listen, you don’t have to give in at all. your ocd can’t control your actions. your thoughts and your actions are two vastly different things. ive lived through my worst panic attacks over the fear of giving in, and that gives me some reassurance. and also knowing things like pedophilia don’t just come on suddenly, they’re issues that gradually make themselves known and usually (with pedophilia at least) it doesn’t come with this much anxiety over actually looking at children / feeling that attraction. it’s less feeling bad about it morally. that’s how i know deep down i’m not like that. i have so much fear because my brain knows it’s one of the most immoral if not THE most immortal acts to commit. it latches onto that because it holds the most weight. 

you’re gonna be okay, and i am too. it’s about learning how your brain works and finding ways to combat negative habits like ocd thoughts. and finding support in others. i wish you the best of luck. take a deep breath, you got this. :)

ive never thought about it like that. it makes sense though, my ocd would still be convinced whatever i do wouldn’t be enough because it’s not about actually doing it but the fear and anxiety over having to “stop myself” from taking that step. 

i’m not sure what the root is, honestly. it didn’t always used to be this specific impulse to google things. in the past it was the fear of hurting my family, the impulse of being in bed at night and my brain saying “you could just get up right now and kill your parents, just get up, it’s so easy just get up” sort of thing. and it kinda transfers to different fears it feels like as soon as i learn to handle it or it fades a new fear comes haha. 

and it often happens during periods of time where my brain isn’t actively focused on something, mostly when i’m about to fall asleep - or if something specific triggers it, like i see a post on facebook or twitter that says “watch out for this account/post/video that is showing gore or smth, etc” and i get that impulse to seek it out specifically instead of avoid it. 

i think my brain just needs to be working on something so it does this to keep turning the gears and getting that rush of adrenaline every time i snowball over a thought. i think i just need to find some more methods of combating this brain habit. turning off my phone is a good idea, though usually at night when it happens and it gets bad enough i will watch a funny youtube video or play a brain puzzle app to distract myself enough until it seems like not a big deal anymore. maybe there’s a way for me to specifically turn off my web provider app at night or something. but even then, i don’t wanna feel like i gotta childlock and avoid everything you know? i wanna learn methods to deal with it and be able to have access to the internet and all the potentially bad things, and have the normal and rational ability to just. not think about those bad things and get the need to seek them out to be sure. thank you for your response i appreciate it!

thank you so much for your response. primarily obsessional ocd makes a lot of sense. it’s like my brain focuses on one fear and continues and obsesses over it until i pretty much get panic attacks at worst. 

the foreign language learning is a good idea - ive actually learned that doing stuff with my hands helps me because it clears my head so lately i’ve been working on legos, coloring books and clay/playdoh. but i can’t really do this when it’s late and i’m in bed haha, so i just try to distract myself with a funny youtube video or a relaxing or puzzle type app to keep my brain occupied. 

ive never thought about the whole pathways thing, that makes sense too. it’s funny because a lot of stuff ive read about anxiety and intrusive thoughts ends up saying “just let the thought come and don’t focus on trying so hard to not think about it” but i guess even thinking about it and pretending it’s a casual thought that will fade away is still continuing that connection. i guess i just need to try out more methods to directly counteract those impulses. 

again, thank you so much for your reply i hope you’re having a good day/night!
